newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH to spend NZ$313 million on upgrade.
newsitem.headline: CHH to spend NZ$313 million on upgrade.

text.p: Forestry group Carter Holt Harvey Ltd said on Friday it would spend NZ$313 million on a major upgrade of its Kinleith mill in the North Island.

CHH said this would result in a 30 percent increase in total production to 600,000 tonnes a year. Of that additional production, 80,000 tonnes would be in market pulp and 70,000 tonnes would be in containerboard. Project time is 18 months.
As part of the project, CHH would shut down its No.5 machine, resulting in a workforce reduction of about 150.

Most of the reductions would not occur until late in the project in 1998. "This is obviously one of the most regrettable aspects of the project, but it is essential for Kinleith to have a viable future," Pulp and Paper Chief Executive George O'Brien said at a presentation to unveil the upgrade.
Kinleith would become significantly more efficient and more productive and would be well-positioned among the most competitive pulp and containerboard mills in the global pulp and paper industry.
The upgrade involves a major rebuild of the No.6 paper machine, the construction of a new 100,000 tonne recycled paper plant and a speed up and enhancement of its No.2 drier.
Additional production would be targeted mainly at Asian markets and CHH expected a substantial amount would be taken up by existing customers.
O'Brien said he expected most of the job losses to come from attrition and voluntary redundancy.
The project would add 70,000 tonnes to its existing 140,000-tonne wastepaper recycling capacity.
CHH Chief Executive John Faraci said CHH's goal was to position itself as a forest products industry leader in the Southern Hemisphere.
CHH is just over 50 percent owned by International Paper . -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
